title: 'I'm Not For A Blank Check': GOP Senator Blasts Sean Duffy's $50 Billion Request
text:

 Anthony Orrico Wed, 18 November 2026 at 2:57 am UTC 2 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Sen. Rand Paul (R-Ky.) on Tuesday railed against Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy 's request for $50 billion  to overhaul the Federal Aviation Administration in the wake of last week's nationwide ground stop. 
 Paul told Fox News' Martha MacCallum that he opposed dolling out the money before a definitive cause of the incident had been identified. 
 News: GOP Senator Directly Contradicts Trump's $2,000 Check Idea 
 "Let's figure out what went wrong. I don't think they technologically completely understand what the problem is yet, so that needs to be explored. Of the $12.5 billion they got last year, they have only spent a billion or two, so there is a lot of money left," Paul said. 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The $12.5 billion was included in President Donald Trump 's "One Big Beautiful Bill Act," but Senate Majority Leader John Thune told reporters on Monday that much of that funding hasn't been spent yet. 
 Paul said he would support passing legislation to remove some of the restrictions on existing funding. 
 "I'm not for a blank check of $50 billion, but why don't we preempt the $3 billion they already have and let them spend that appropriately?" Paul said. 
 Politics: Sean Duffy 'Can't Apologize' For Nationwide Flight Nightmare... But Still Begs For Billions 
 Several other Republicans in Congress also expressed skepticism about Duffy's request, even after the secretary met with GOP senators on Tuesday. 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "I don't think the full $50 billion will be funded. Some of that is not safety-related," said Sen. Ted Cruz (R-Texas).
 "We're not going to give them $50 billion," said Sen. John Kennedy (R-La.). "But I think that we are willing to provide the money to replace the copper wires with fiber optics, and to try to stop the bleeding."
